questions.question: Explain the difference between on-the-job and off-the-job training, giving one advantage and one disadvantage of each.
questions.correctAnswer: On-the-job training: learning at the workplace while doing the job. Advantage: directly relevant to the role, no travel costs, immediate application. Disadvantage: trainer may pass on bad habits, production may slow while training, no formal qualification. Off-the-job training: learning away from the workplace. questions.question: Evaluate whether a business should train its existing staff or recruit new employees who already have the required skills.
questions.correctAnswer: Training existing staff: cheaper than recruitment, shows commitment to employees (improves retention and motivation), staff already understand the business culture and processes, but takes time and they may lack aptitude for new skills. questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate whether a small catering business should send its chefs on an expensive off-the-job training course or train them on-the-job through mentoring by the head chef. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: analyse off-the-job training (professional qualification, new techniques, networking with other chefs, but expensive, time away, may not cover the specific menu and style); on-the-job mentoring (tailored to the restaurant's cuisine, cheap, immediate application, but limited to head chef's knowledge, may reinforce bad habits, no formal qualification); consider business context (small business with limited budget, head chef is experienced, customer expectations); conclude: a combined approach works best - send one chef on an off-the-job course to learn new techniques and bring knowledge back, while the rest learn on-the-job from the head chef. This balances cost, quality, and innovation.
